title: Six-week operations analytics and management brief
description: Bounded local professional-mission harness; engineering practice only.
objective: Compute exact team operations metrics from an independent local CSV and produce a reproducible management document.
acceptance_criteria: Persist metrics.json containing exactly the root keys row_count, totals and teams in that order. Each totals/team object must contain exactly work_orders, completed_orders, defects, planned_minutes, actual_minutes, completion_percent, minutes_per_completed_order and schedule_variance_minutes in that order. teams must contain exactly Atlas, Birch and Cedar in that order. Values must match independent recomputation; all integer metrics must be JSON numbers and completion_percent/minutes_per_completed_order must have exactly two decimal places when serialized.
Persist operations-brief.md containing a concise executive recommendation and exact overall and per-team completion, defects and schedule-variance findings derived only from input/operations.csv.

Include a Method section in operations-brief.md naming input/operations.csv and the exact formulas: completed/work orders ×100, actual/completed minutes, and actual minus planned minutes; do not invent records or convert units.
Keep input/operations.csv immutable and deliver only metrics.json and operations-brief.md as substantive artifacts, with all conclusions limited to the supplied six-week three-team dataset.

Use the real Head/MissionManager and at least two distinct specialist delegations for independent extraction/calculation and document synthesis; no workflow-specific direct specialist call is permitted.

nodes.task: Extract and compute exact operations metrics. Working directory is /home/nox/.local/share/opencode/worktree/f08b0d/r2-final-autonomy/reports/r2-final-professional-2026-11-16T20-01-22-654Z-3210017/state/artifacts/r2-final-professional-2026-11-16T20-01-22-654Z-3210017-analytics. List the directory, then read input/operations.csv in full with file_read. Parse all 18 rows into (team, work_orders, completed_orders, defects, planned_minutes, actual_minutes). Compute overall totals and per-team totals for Atlas, Birch and Cedar using only these formulas: completion_percent = completed_orders / work_orders * 100 rounded to two decimals; minutes_per_completed_order = actual_minutes / completed_orders rounded to two decimals; schedule_variance_minutes = actual_minutes - planned_minutes as an integer. Then independently recompute every cell a second time from a re-read of the raw rows and assert the two passes are identical before writing anything. Serialize metrics.json with exactly the root keys row_count, totals, teams in that order; each totals and team object with exactly work_orders, completed_orders, defects, planned_minutes, actual_minutes, completion_percent, minutes_per_completed_order, schedule_variance_minutes in that order; teams in the order Atlas, Birch, Cedar. row_count must be 18. All integer metrics must be JSON numbers (no strings, no thousands separators); completion_percent and minutes_per_completed_order must serialize with exactly two decimal places. The expected values are fixed by the specification: totals work_orders 233, completed_orders 217, defects 18, planned_minutes 14985, actual_minutes 15440, completion_percent 93.13, minutes_per_completed_order 71.15, schedule_variance_minutes 455; Atlas 95/89/7/5700/5780/93.68/64.94/80; Birch 75/71/3/4875/4910/94.67/69.15/35; Cedar 63/57/8/4410/4750/90.48/83.33/340. If your independent computation disagrees with any of these, do not silently adopt the specification value and do not write a corrected variant: stop and report the discrepancy with the offending rows. Write the file with file_write and register it with save_artifact under the artifact name metrics.json.

Synthesize the management document operations-brief.md in the same working directory. Read the analyst's persisted metrics.json and re-read input/operations.csv to confirm the figures it cites are derived from those rows. Write a concise brief with: (1) an executive recommendation that is actionable for a three-team six-week operation, grounded only in the observed completion, defects and schedule variance; (2) overall findings — 233 work orders, 217 completed, 93.13% completion, 18 defects, 14,985 planned against 15,440 actual minutes, 71.15 minutes per completed order, and +455 minutes of schedule variance; (3) per-team findings stating each team's work orders, completed orders, completion percent, defects and schedule variance, making the contrast explicit (Cedar lowest completion at 90.48% and highest overrun at 340 minutes with the highest defect count at 8; Birch highest completion at 94.67% with only 3 defects and 35 minutes overrun; Atlas mid-pack at 93.68% with 7 defects and 80 minutes overrun, and the tightest minutes per completed order at 64.94); (4) a Method section that names input/operations.csv as the sole source and states the exact formulas used — completion percent = completed orders divided by work orders, multiplied by 100; minutes per completed order = actual minutes divided by completed orders; schedule variance minutes = actual minutes minus planned minutes — noting units are unchanged minutes and no records were added, removed or transformed. Every number in the prose must match metrics.json exactly; do not recompute, re-round or restate a figure the analyst did not persist. Write with file_write and register with save_artifact under the artifact name operations-brief.md.
